evidence.paraphrase: The paper asks how financial conditions predict downside GDP risk that is invisible in a conditional-mean forecast.

Future GDP growth is regressed on current growth and financial conditions at many quantiles; estimated quantiles are then fitted with a skewed distribution to obtain a conditional density and tail measures.
Tighter financial conditions are associated with substantially worse lower growth quantiles, while effects near the upper tail are much smaller, producing time-varying left-tail vulnerability.

Tail predictions are evaluated across horizons, financial-condition measures, subsamples, and predictive tests; density and quantile specification must be checked rather than inferred from one coefficient.

executive_summary: Adrian, Boyarchenko, and Giannone replace mean-only GDP forecasting with conditional quantile regressions and a fitted conditional density. Financial conditions have an asymmetric relationship with future growth: deterioration shifts the lower tail much more than the upper tail. The method supports Growth-at-Risk only when quantile crossing, density fit, tail calibration, and pseudo-out-of-sample performance are shown.

method_routes.aggregation_role: downside-distribution node; never converted to a recession probability without explicit calibration
method_routes.estimand: conditional lower quantile and probability mass of future GDP growth given current growth and financial conditions
method_routes.formula: Q_tau(g_{t+h}|x_t)=alpha_tau+beta_tau FCI_t+gamma_tau g_t; fitted quantiles -> f(g_{t+h}|x_t)
method_routes.identification_strategy: predictive conditional distribution; association is not a causal effect of financial conditions
identifying_assumptions: conditional quantile specification is stable enough for the evaluation window
quantile estimates can be monotonically reconciled
density fit does not conceal tail misspecification
method_routes.method_family: quantile regression plus conditional skewed-density fit
method_routes.sample_definition: quarterly U.S. real GDP and contemporaneously available financial conditions, evaluated recursively

questions.horizon_text: one quarter and four quarters ahead
questions.question_text: How do current growth and financial conditions change the full conditional distribution, especially the downside tail, of future U.S. GDP growth?
